summary: Mission Architect is a free, browser-based game where kids ages 7–12 become the chief engineer of a space mission. Players choose a target (the Moon, Mars, an asteroid or Jupiter’s moon Europa), then pick a rocket, spacecraft, power source, antenna and science instruments. Six live meters (budget, weight, power, data, science and success odds) show the cost of every choice, so no option is free. For example, solar panels give only 28 W at Europa, while a nuclear battery gives 150 W but costs more. After launch, a short simulation with random events shows whether the design survives, then gives a score and a tip for trying again. It needs no download or account.
details:
What it does: Players design a mission in seven steps (mission, rocket, spacecraft, power, comms, science, launch) and then watch it fly. Instant warnings explain problems in plain language, such as “Short by 222 W. Instruments will slow down.”

Impact: Kids feel real engineering trade-offs (budget vs weight vs power vs data) instead of reading about them. Failed launches give a tip, so players learn and retry.

Creativity: A design-then-launch loop with random events (solar flare, micrometeoroids, antenna glitch) and four very different missions makes each playthrough different.

Science: Sunlight follows the inverse-square law (Mars about 43%, Europa about 4% of Earth-orbit sunlight). Radiation risk is highest at Europa, data links weaken with distance, and the favoured instruments echo NASA’s Europa Clipper. These are simplified teaching values built into the game, not live NASA data.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (canvas animation), as one page hosted on Netlify. Works on phones and tablets, with keyboard-operable cards and reduced-motion support.

SI use: Claude (Anthropic) was used to help write the game’s code and to create the demo slide deck. The team chose the concept and mission design and tested the game. The game page and its metadata acknowledge the AI assistance.
dataRefs: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer (brief and resources)
